simple.meaning: הַלָּז (hallâz) is a Hebrew word meaning “this or that.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: הַלָּז (H1975) appears 7 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Judges 6:20, with occurrences in Judges, 1 Samuel, 2 Kings, Daniel, Zechariah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הַלָּז (H1975) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in הַלָּז (H1975) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: הַלָּז (hallâz) / H1975 is traced through Judges 6:20, 1 Samuel 14:1, 1 Samuel 17:26, 2 Kings 4:25 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: The angel of God said to him, “Take the meat and the unleavened cakes, and lay them on this rock, and pour out the broth.”

timeline.evidenceText: The angel of God said to him, “Take the meat and the unleavened cakes, and lay them on this rock, and pour out the broth.”

Now it fell on a day, that Jonathan the son of Saul said to the young man who bore his armor, “Come! Let’s go over to the Philistines’ garrison that is on the other side.” But he didn’t tell his father.

David spoke to the men who stood by him, saying, “What shall be done to the man who kills this Philistine, and takes away the reproach from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?”
So she went, and came to the man of God to Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her afar off, he said to Gehazi his servant, “Behold, there is the Shunammite.
Then he said, “What monument is that which I see?”
I heard a man’s voice between the banks of the Ulai, which called, and said, “Gabriel, make this man understand the vision.”
For Yahweh of Armies says: ‘For honor he has sent me to the nations which plundered you; for he who touches you touches the apple of his eye.

definitions.full: H1975. hallaz הַלָּז pronoun common this , a rare synonym of זֶה or הַזֶּה , this (Arabic (also ), plural , who, which (compare זֶה , which is used also sometimes as relative), formed from , the definite article, and the pronoun זוּ זֶה, , with the insertion of the demonstrative element la , and thus in fact = הַזֶּה : W AGi. § 347, CG p. 117 ) — usually with a substantive defined by the article, Judg 6:20 הַלָּז הַסֶּלַע this rock, 1Sam 14:1 הַלָּז מֵעֵבֶר off this side-across, 17:26 הַלָּז אֶתהַֿמְּלִשְׁתִּי , (+ 20:19 ᵐ5 Th We Dr τὸ ἐργαβ ἐκεῖνο , i.e. (or הַלָּאז ) הַלָּז הָאַרְגָּב this mound ( or cairn), for האזל האבן ) 2Kin 23:17 ; Zech 2:8 ; with a feminine , 2Kin 4:25 הַלּז הַשּׁוּנַמִּית : without a substantive Dan 8:16 לְהַלָּז to this one (= normal לָזֶה ).
